{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Combined",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor (5 levels). Given extreme right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), apply log-transformation or use robust ANOVA. Welch's ANOVA recommended due to likely variance heterogeneity (Sham mean=4.68, SD likely inflated).",
    "For Success: Binary outcome makes standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or Cochran-Armitage trend test if ordering hypothesized. Report odds ratios versus Sham reference.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with caution. Distribution is severely right-skewed (max=29.82, mean=0.47). Log-transformation essential; consider Gamma GLM or permutation ANOVA as alternative.",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA feasible but check variance homogeneity. Distribution appears reasonable (mean=12.50, SD=4.46, max=75.35) with moderate right tail. Welch's ANOVA or robust methods preferred.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA on raw or arcsine-square-root transformed scale. Bounded [0,1] variable with mean=0.38, SD=0.24; Beta regression or arcsin-sqrt transformation recommended over standard ANOVA due to bounded support."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed from experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice using autocorrelation function on residuals.",
    "Normality: Shapiro-Wilk or Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests per group; Q-Q plots mandatory given extreme skew in Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test and Brown-Forsythe test. Expected violation due to Sham group's distinct performance profile (lower success, higher time-to-target, lower AD).",
    "Sample size balance: Severe imbalance—Combined n=48846 (64%) versus Sham n=3505 (4.6%). Weighted least squares or mixed-effects models with random intercept for Mouse may improve inference.",
    "Outlier assessment: Identify trials with Time-to-Target >20s or Path Efficiency >10 for sensitivity analyses."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant: Pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Average Speed, transformed AD), or Games-Howell if variances unequal.",
    "For Success (logistic): Pairwise odds ratios with Bonferroni-Holm correction for 10 comparisons.",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs ICMS Only (additive vs single-modality), Combined vs Bright Visual Only, Combined vs Dim Visual Only (intensity comparison), all active conditions vs Sham.",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d for continuous variables (pooled SD or Sham-referenced), odds ratios for Success.",
    "Visualization: Group means with 95% CIs, violin plots showing distributions, and letter-coded groupings from compact letter display."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: lowest Success (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236) indicating most directed paths or failure to explore.",
    "Combined and Bright Visual Only expected highest Success (~0.78-0.79), with Combined showing fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s) and highest AD (0.399) suggesting more variable/exploratory trajectories when sensory information is rich.",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only intermediate: Success ~0.67-0.69, Time-to-Target ~3.0-3.1s, Path Efficiency ~0.43, suggesting single-modality stimulation improves over Sham but underperforms combined or bright visual conditions.",
    "Paradigm effects likely largest for Success and Time-to-Target given Sham's dramatic underperformance; Average Speed effects more modest (range 10.7-12.8); AD may distinguish sensory-rich from sensory-poor conditions."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Massive sample size imbalance: Combined dominates (64% of data), reducing precision for Sham comparisons and inflating apparent statistical significance.",
    "Repeated measures structure ignored: 8 mice with 7,233-10,986 trials each; mouse-level clustering unaccounted for in simple ANOVA, risking inflated Type I error.",
    "Success is binary: ANOVA entirely inappropriate; logistic or mixed-effects logistic regression required.",
    "Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target extreme outliers: single-factor ANOVA means may be driven by tail behavior rather than typical performance.",
    "No temporal information: learning effects, fatigue, or session structure unknown from current data view.",
    "AD bounded [0,1]: Standard ANOVA assumes unbounded response; transformation or specialized model needed."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMM) with random intercept for Mouse for continuous outcomes, and generalized linear mixed models (GLMM, binomial family) for Success. Use Stim Paradigm as fixed effect with Helmert or custom contrasts comparing Combined to constituent modalities and all active to Sham. Apply bootstrap confidence intervals for group differences given distributional concerns. For Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target, consider robust MM-estimation or quantile regression to characterize median rather than mean differences."
}
